item.title: Obsidian Gains Local REST API with MCP Server for Secure Vault Access
item.description:
Obsidian Gains Local REST API with MCP Server for Secure Vault Access

A new plugin provides a secure REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Obsidian vaults, enabling scripts, browser extensions, and AI agents to interact directly with vault contents.

🔍 Overview

The plugin exposes a secure, authenticated REST API alongside an MCP server, both serving the same core capabilities. All requests are served over HTTPS with a locally generated certificate and gated behind API key authentication.

🧩 How it works

The MCP server runs at https://127.0.0.1:27124/mcp/ and requires a bearer token in the Authorization header. A plain HTTP endpoint is also available at http://127.0.0.1:27123/mcp/ if enabled.

⚙️ Key details

  • Authentication: HTTPS with locally generated certificate, API key authentication, bearer token for MCP clients
  • Certificate: CA is name-constrained to localhost, 127.0.0.1, and configured hostnames; HTTP endpoint available for easier setup
  • Download CA: Certificate authority available at https://127.0.0.1:27134/obsidian-local-rest-api.crt
  • Vault operations: Full CRUD on any file including binary files, surgically patch specific sections (headings, blocks, frontmatter), search with full-text or JsonLogic queries, follow vault events via Server-Sent Events
  • Active file: Read or write the currently open note in Obsidian
  • Commands: List and execute any Obsidian command, query tags with usage counts, open specific files in UI
  • Extensibility: Other plugins can register their own routes via an API extension interface

🚀 Availability

After installing and enabling the plugin, users can find their API key and certificate in Settings → Local REST API.

#Obsidian #RESTAPI #MCP #Vault #Plugin

Source: coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api

item.title: AI Coding Agent Optimized with TokenEconomizer
item.description:
AI Coding Agent Optimized with TokenEconomizer

TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that reduces waste in AI coding agent sessions by learning from past sessions and adapting to future ones.

🔍 Overview

TokenEconomizer is a plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model.
  • TokenEconomizer reads the session’s log and updates what it knows about the repository.
  • Micro-skills capture repository-specific knowledge in one-line notes.
  • Tool pruning removes tools that repository history suggests the agent is unlikely to use, while always retaining core tools for running commands and editing files.
  • Failure-loop intervention watches for an agent that keeps hitting the same failure.

⚙️ Key details

  • TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents on 277 real bug-fixing tasks.
  • Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
  • The agent received 23 tool descriptions on every turn, but 16 were never called.

🚀 Availability

TokenEconomizer is available as an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security.

💡 Why it matters

TokenEconomizer reduces waste without changing the agent or its underlying model, so developers can use it alongside the coding agents they already rely on.

📊 Evaluation

  • TokenEconomizer lowered the average cost by 18.4–30.9% on 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories, using five different AI coding agent and model combinations.
  • The savings also carried over to sequential web development, with costs 16.0–21.2% lower on Web-Bench.
  • On security auditing, where every task is in a new repository, costs were 6.4–19.6% lower.

📸 Images

item.title: AI plugin updates execute_sql output format
item.description:
AI plugin updates execute_sql output format

A new version of the plugin has been released, changing the output format of execute_sql from an array of arrays to an array of objects. This is the first non-alpha release.

🔍 Overview

The plugin now returns rows from execute_sql as an array of objects, improving clarity for weaker models by eliminating ambiguity in positional array elements.

⚙️ Key details

  • Output format: array of objects (previously array of arrays)
  • Dependency: requires mcp>=2.1.1
  • Release status: first non-alpha version

🚀 Availability

The update is ready for use, as confirmed by the developer’s own extensive testing.

#AI #plugin #SQL #outputformat #mcp

Source: Release: datasette-mcp 0.2
